answer: Behavioral lineage graph scoring. Each identity's actions form edges; shared device or timing fingerprints cluster them into a candidate vertex. Post-hoc audit checks whether a cluster's internal coordination exceeds chance, flagging it via a ripple of correlated anomalies across the graph. To pass, an attacker must simulate independent histories with distinct timing and device noise per fake identity—a fable of autonomy that costs real infrastructure and weeks of aged activity per account.
